text.L1: A change can be physical or chemical. The key question is: has a new substance formed?
text.L2: In a physical change, shape, size or state changes, but no new substance forms.
text.L3: Melting ghee is physical. It is still ghee, and it becomes solid again when cooled.
text.L4: Dissolving is also physical. Sugar spreads into water, but it is still there and still has mass.
text.L5: In a chemical change, one or more new substances with different properties are formed.
text.L6: Gas bubbles, a colour change, heat or light, a new smell, or a new solid can be evidence.
text.L7: Here is a common myth: dissolved sugar has disappeared and has no mass. Not true; dissolving does not make the sugar vanish.
text.L8: Baking soda and lemon juice fizz because a new gas forms. That is a chemical change.
